subject: japanese eel
title: These Eels Get Swallowed Whole, Then Escape Through the Gills

scenes.text: Being swallowed whole isn't the end for this eel.
Scientists in Japan let a predatory fish eat young Japanese eels, then filmed inside its stomach with X-rays.
All 32 eels went down. Twenty-eight of them started fighting to get out.
They backed up the fish's throat, tail first, and poked their tails out through its gills.
Then they pulled their heads free. Nine got out, in about 56 seconds on average.
It's the first time anyone has filmed prey moving inside a predator's gut. Eaten, and still not caught.

description:
Young Japanese eels can escape after being swallowed by a fish.
Researchers at Nagasaki University used X-ray video to watch eels inside the predatory fish Odontobutis obscura. Of 32 swallowed eels, 28 tried to escape, 13 got their tails out through the gills and 9 got away completely, backing up the digestive tract tail first. It took about 56 seconds on average. The study appeared in Current Biology in September 2024.
Which animal has the best escape trick?
first_comment: It took the team a year to get clear X-ray footage. Thirteen eels got their tails out, but only nine made it all the way. Would you bet on the eel?
